known_gaps.title: The committed rung-1 verdict contradicts the 2026-10-01 report
known_gaps.detail: gate-20261001-M01-linux-0001.md section 5.1 quotes a rung-1 verdict of PASS with A p50 1.377, B p50 0.816, C p50 1.362. No artifact in the repository, the sandbox, or the CI logs contains those numbers. The committed verdict file says BUDGET FAIL with A p50 1.544, B p50 1.159, C p50 2.105.
known_gaps.consequence: The claim that rung 1 passes, repeated in HANDOFF.md section 1.4 and HANDOFF.json gate_history.verdicts, is not supported by the committed evidence.

known_gaps.title: The Android tier has never been measured
known_gaps.detail: Rung 1's recovery was measured on a 4-core desktop CPU. The Android tier is unmeasured and no reference device exists in this environment.

known_gaps.title: The per-scenario summaries are not committed
known_gaps.detail: .gitignore excludes everything under BenchmarkResults/ except verdict_*.txt. The summary_*.json files and the NUnit results_*.xml exist only on the machine that produced them.
known_gaps.consequence: The verdict files are the only committed evidence and carry no host metadata, no per-scenario mass figures and no determinism hashes.

known_gaps.title: The thresholds are mirrored in two places
known_gaps.detail: Tools/bench_thresholds.json and BenchmarkScenarios.cs both hold them. The harness writes the values it used into every summary, so drift is visible in results rather than inferred.

known_gaps.title: The quietness instrumentation is committed but has never been attached to a verdict
known_gaps.detail: run_bench.sh now samples /proc/stat twice and writes BenchmarkResults/quietness_<tier>.txt with the core count, both busy fractions, the wall clock, the load average and a quiet/noisy/BUSY verdict. It has only been exercised on the failed no-editor run, where it reported 22.2% busy (10.7 of 48 cores) under loadavg 10.81.
known_gaps.consequence: WAS: no quietness was recorded at all. NOW: quietness is recorded, but the rung-0 and rung-1 verdicts predate it and still carry no machine state. They remain unattributable.

known_gaps.title: No Unity editor exists in the environment the rung-2 revision was written in
known_gaps.detail: /opt/unity/Editor/Unity is absent, there is no dotnet, no mono and no docker in the sandbox. The C# added by this revision has never been compiled, and the rung-2 benchmark has never been run, in any environment.
known_gaps.consequence: The rung-2 implementation is unverified. A compile error in WaterWindow.cs or ActiveWindowConfig.cs would not be caught until a machine with the editor runs the gate.

known_gaps.title: The benchmark world cannot measure the tile mechanism the rung names
known_gaps.detail: The harness reports tile_count = 4 as a 2x2 grid. In a 2x2 world the active-tile set at radius 1 is 4 of 4, so rung 2's tile selection saves nothing there.
known_gaps.consequence: Even with an editor, a rung-2 verdict from this harness measures the cell scope only. The tile mechanism needs a larger benchmark world.

known_gaps.title: The CI gate uploads a verdict artifact even when it produces no verdict
known_gaps.detail: Run 30 (2026-10-08) produced no verdict: the checker exited 3, INPUT ERROR, having found no summaries and no results XML. The 'Upload the verdict' step nevertheless uploaded a file, because BenchmarkResults/verdict_linux.txt is COMMITTED to the repository - the checkout supplies it and the step copies whatever is there. The artifact water-gate-verdict-linux-<sha>.zip is 631 bytes compressed and holds verdict_linux.txt at 1034 bytes, md5 77d5a170189e46f0c2b1c4097d679641, byte-identical to the committed rung-0 verdict (blob 179076dd). It is named for run 30's own head SHA, ae5a93ae.
known_gaps.consequence: A reviewer or an automated consumer reading water-gate-verdict-linux-ae5a93ae... sees a full scenario table and 'VERDICT: BUDGET FAIL' and can attribute it to a run that never measured anything. The build is correctly red (exit 3 fails the build); it is the ARTIFACT that lies.
known_gaps.recommended_fix: Gate the upload on the checker's exit code (upload only when it is 0 or 1), or delete the checked-out verdict before the benchmark step so an artifact can only ever be freshly written. State the artifact's provenance in the job summary either way.

rung_2.label: active water window
rung_2.why_not_measured: No Unity editor exists in the environment this revision was written in: /opt/unity/Editor/Unity is absent and run_bench.sh now refuses to start without it. No benchmark number here was measured on any machine.

frozen_untouched.note: Blob prefixes, unchanged by this revision, as required.

implementation.mechanism: WaterSolver.Step skips any cell outside a Chebyshev window in all four passes. Pass 1 clears flux globally and a windowed-out cell never re-populates it, so no flux crosses the boundary and the step is a closed system over the active set. A cell outside the window is never assigned, so it holds its last depth.
implementation.data_driven: Scope, radius and origin are configuration, read from PET_BENCH_WINDOW_SCOPE / PET_BENCH_WINDOW_RADIUS. Scope=none is the identity, which is how rungs 0 and 1 stay reproducible from one tree.

window_scope_semantics.none: every cell of every tile steps - the identity path rungs 0 and 1 take
window_scope_semantics.tiles: a tile steps only if within r tiles of the camera's tile; per-tile cost unchanged
window_scope_semantics.cells: cells within r cells of the camera's cell step; per-tile cost reduced
window_scope_semantics.note: The rung as named by the ladder is TILE-based. The cell scope exists because the harness allocates one tile per scenario, so a per-tile step cost is the only thing it can measure.

tile_grid.note: In a 2x2 world radius 1 covers every tile, so rung 2's TILE mechanism has zero effect in the benchmark world. The 7.11x reduction is a property of the shipping 8x8 slice and the harness cannot measure it as built.

model.assumption: W scales with the cell count of the tile
model.solved_for: S, the per-step cost that does not scale with the active set
model.fit_inputs: the committed rung-0 and rung-1 p50 values for each scenario
model.identifiability: Two points and two unknowns, so the fit is exact by construction and is NOT evidence that the model is right. It is falsifiable: a real rung-2 verdict can be diffed against it.
model.formula: T = S + W(res) * active_fraction;  S = (4*T129 - T257) / 3
model.confidence: Low. Two points fit two unknowns exactly, so the fit is not evidence the model is right. The only independent support is the sublinear rung 0 -> 1 scaling, which is consistent with a nonzero fixed term.

rung_2.key_finding: At a radius-1 cell window the windowed term is 9 cells of 16641, so the modelled cost collapses to the fixed term S. Rung 2's modelled floor is S, not zero. C_FastForward carries S = 1.116 ms, which is 74% of the 1.500 ms p50 threshold spent before any water moves. That is the number to watch when a real measurement exists.
rung_2.benchmark_blind_spot: The benchmark world is 2x2 tiles, so every tile is within 1 of every other and rung 2's tile saving there is exactly 1.0x. The 7.11x figure is a property of the shipping 8x8 slice (64 tiles -> 9 active) and cannot be observed until the harness steps more than one tile.
rung_2.not_a_game_configuration: A radius-1 cell window freezes 99.95% of the tile. It is a pinhole, not a playable setting. The modelled pass means 'rung 2 is worth measuring', not 'rung 2 passes'.
